results.raw:
Creating a comprehensive URL map is the foundational step in managing your website's redirects effectively. This map serves as a crucial reference document, detailing every old address and its intended new destination. It is important to clearly delineate what the map represents. The URL map records the old addresses and their planned new destinations. This document outlines the strategy for moving users from outdated links to their correct, current locations.

Separating the map from actual redirect testing is vital for accurate analysis. A planned destination listed in your map is not definitive proof that the redirect mechanism is functioning correctly. You must test the old address and the final destination page as two distinct actions. Do not assume success based solely on the map's entry. This separation allows you to isolate whether the link itself is broken or if the server-side redirect is executing as expected.

When testing, maintain strict objectivity. Record the observed test result for each old URL and its corresponding final page separately. If a test fails, record it as a failed test requiring follow-up investigation, rather than marking it as completed. Avoid inventing statistics, promising rankings, or creating fabricated URLs. Focus only on the verifiable outcome of the redirect process to ensure your data remains accurate and actionable.
